extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act establishes that high-risk AI providers may use one of two conformity assessment routes: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII.

Annex VII (third-party notified body assessment) is mandatory for high-risk AI systems involving biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems; most other high-risk systems may use the Annex VI self-assessment route.

For high-risk AI systems already covered by existing EU product-safety legislation listed in Annex I Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the conformity assessment procedures of that sectoral legislation, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with the AI-specific requirements.

A provider may choose any notified body for the Annex VII procedure, except that where a high-risk AI system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities, or EU institutions/bodies, the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body.
Substantial modifications to a high-risk AI system require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in systems designed to continue learning after deployment.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to derogate from the standard conformity assessment procedure and authorise market placement of a specific high-risk AI system for a limited period, for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life and health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructure assets.
Article 35 of the AI Act establishes the system for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies.
Notified bodies designated under EU legislation (including potentially the AI Act) are to be listed in the Commission's NANDO (New Approach Notified and Designated Organisations) information system.

As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 notified bodies designated under the Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) and 19 under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR); these are sectoral designations, not AI Act-specific.
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem specifically for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and capacity described as limited.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act in the medical-device/SaMD context.

High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act are set to fully apply from August 2026, after which notified bodies designated under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments.

A 2025/2026 proposal (COM(2025) 836, referenced in Council document ST-15708-2025-INIT and ST-7322-2026-INIT) would add a new Annex XIV listing codes/categories for AI systems to structure NANDO designation of conformity assessment bodies under a provision numbered Article 30, and would amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements.

Under the earlier 2022 negotiating proposal text of Article 43, providers of Annex III point 1 (biometric) high-risk systems applying harmonised standards or common specifications could choose between listed assessment procedures.

Notified bodies may, under Annex VII, be granted access to training and trained models of a high-risk AI system (including parameters) where necessary and after other verification means have proven insufficient, subject to IP and confidentiality protections.

contradictions.claim_a: The AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) Article 43 and Annex VI/VII framework for conformity assessment and notified bodies is adopted, binding law already structuring high-risk AI compliance.
contradictions.claim_b: A separate 2025/2026 Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) proposes adding a new Annex XIV and an Article 30-based designation scheme for conformity assessment bodies in NANDO, suggesting the detailed designation framework for AI Act notified bodies is still in the proposal stage, not yet adopted.
contradictions.description: Sources treat the Article 43/Annex VI-VII framework as settled law, while other sources (8, 9) describe a still-pending legislative proposal to establish the detailed classification/designation codes (Annex XIV, Article 30) needed for notified bodies to actually be designated under NANDO, indicating the designation infrastructure itself may not yet be finalized even though the underlying conformity assessment obligation is in force.

open_issues: No source confirms, as of the current date (October 2026), how many notified bodies have actually been designated specifically under the EU AI Act (as opposed to MDR/IVDR or other sectoral regimes); the most recent dated sources are from March–June 2026 and report zero or near-zero AI Act-specific designations.

It is unclear whether the proposed new Annex XIV and Article 30 designation-code system (COM(2025) 836) has been formally adopted, and how it relates procedurally to the existing Article 35 notified-body listing mechanism already in the AI Act.

The sources do not clarify whether the August 2026 'full application' deadline for high-risk obligations has been met with sufficient notified body capacity, given Article 46 derogation exists for cases where conformity assessment cannot be completed through normal channels.
No source provides a definitive, current list of named notified bodies designated under the AI Act (by name, Member State, or scope/code), unlike the detailed MDR/IVDR counts available via NANDO.

It is unclear how the Annex I Section A sectoral conformity assessment route (e.g., medical devices, machinery) is coordinated in practice with the AI Act's own Annex VI/VII procedures when both regimes apply to the same product.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act and Notified Body Designation Status

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems—internal control (Annex VI) or third-party notified body assessment (Annex VII)—with the latter mandatory for certain biometric and critical-infrastructure systems (low confidence). However, the infrastructure for actually designating AI Act-specific notified bodies appears incomplete: as of early-to-mid 2026, sources report few or no formally designated bodies, and a legislative proposal to create the classification framework needed for designations (new Annex XIV, Article 30) was still pending (low-to-medium confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 of the AI Act permits high-risk AI providers to choose between internal control under Annex VI or third-party assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). Some sources suggest Annex VII third-party assessment is mandatory specifically for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure systems, with most other high-risk systems eligible for Annex VI self-assessment (low confidence) ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment), [sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)).

For high-risk AI systems already regulated under existing EU product-safety legislation listed in Annex I Section A—such as medical devices and machinery—providers must follow the conformity assessment procedures of that sectoral legislation, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

Providers generally may select any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except where the AI system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions—in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs the notified-body role (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications generally trigger a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously-learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 allows market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard procedures and authorize temporary market placement for exceptional public-security, health, environmental, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Under Annex VII, notified bodies may be granted access to training data and trained model parameters where necessary, subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
Article 35 establishes the system for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)), with designated bodies to appear in the Commission's NANDO database (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex MDR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02017R0745-20260101)). As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 notified bodies under the Medical Devices Regulation and 19 under the IVDR—sectoral designations unrelated to the AI Act itself (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex evaluation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)).

Specifically for the AI Act, sources indicate the notified body ecosystem was still under construction as of March 2026, with designation processes ongoing and capacity limited (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)), and as of April 2026 no notified bodies had been formally designated in the medical-device/SaMD context (low confidence) ([aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). High-risk obligations are set to fully apply from August 2026, after which AI Act-designated notified bodies are expected to begin conducting assessments (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [mdxcro.com](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)).

A 2025/2026 legislative proposal (COM(2025) 836) would add a new Annex XIV and an Article 30 provision to structure NANDO designation codes for AI conformity assessment bodies, and would amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act requirements (medium confidence) ([Council document ST-7322-2026-INIT](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf), [ST-15708-2025-INIT](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A notable tension exists between sources presenting the Article 43/Annex VI-VII framework as fully operational law and sources (medium confidence) describing the designation infrastructure (Annex XIV, Article 30 codes) as still pending legislative adoption—suggesting the conformity assessment obligation is legally in force while the practical mechanism to designate bodies may not yet be finalized. Several low-confidence claims (0.12–0.24) regarding notified body designation timelines and the Annex VII mandatory-use scope should be treated cautiously, as they rely on undated industry blogs rather than authoritative legal text.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source confirms how many notified bodies have been formally designated specifically under the AI Act as of the current date. It remains unclear whether COM(2025) 836 has been adopted and how it relates to the existing Article 35 mechanism. The interplay between Annex I sectoral conformity assessment (e.g., MDR) and AI Act-specific Annex VI/VII procedures for dual-regulated products requires further clarification, as does whether notified body capacity will be sufficient by the August 2026 deadline.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act and Notified Body Designation Status

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems—internal control (Annex VI) or third-party notified body assessment (Annex VII)—with the latter mandatory for certain biometric and critical-infrastructure systems (low confidence). However, the infrastructure for actually designating AI Act-specific notified bodies appears incomplete: as of early-to-mid 2026, sources report few or no formally designated bodies, and a legislative proposal to create the classification framework needed for designations (new Annex XIV, Article 30) was still pending (low-to-medium confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 of the AI Act permits high-risk AI providers to choose between internal control under Annex VI or third-party assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). Some sources suggest Annex VII third-party assessment is mandatory specifically for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure systems, with most other high-risk systems eligible for Annex VI self-assessment (low confidence) ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment), [sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)).

For high-risk AI systems already regulated under existing EU product-safety legislation listed in Annex I Section A—such as medical devices and machinery—providers must follow the conformity assessment procedures of that sectoral legislation, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

Providers generally may select any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except where the AI system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions—in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs the notified-body role (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications generally trigger a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously-learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 allows market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard procedures and authorize temporary market placement for exceptional public-security, health, environmental, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Under Annex VII, notified bodies may be granted access to training data and trained model parameters where necessary, subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
Article 35 establishes the system for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)), with designated bodies to appear in the Commission's NANDO database (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex MDR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02017R0745-20260101)). As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 notified bodies under the Medical Devices Regulation and 19 under the IVDR—sectoral designations unrelated to the AI Act itself (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex evaluation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)).

Specifically for the AI Act, sources indicate the notified body ecosystem was still under construction as of March 2026, with designation processes ongoing and capacity limited (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)), and as of April 2026 no notified bodies had been formally designated in the medical-device/SaMD context (low confidence) ([aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). High-risk obligations are set to fully apply from August 2026, after which AI Act-designated notified bodies are expected to begin conducting assessments (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [mdxcro.com](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)).

A 2025/2026 legislative proposal (COM(2025) 836) would add a new Annex XIV and an Article 30 provision to structure NANDO designation codes for AI conformity assessment bodies, and would amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act requirements (medium confidence) ([Council document ST-7322-2026-INIT](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf), [ST-15708-2025-INIT](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A notable tension exists between sources presenting the Article 43/Annex VI-VII framework as fully operational law and sources (medium confidence) describing the designation infrastructure (Annex XIV, Article 30 codes) as still pending legislative adoption—suggesting the conformity assessment obligation is legally in force while the practical mechanism to designate bodies may not yet be finalized. Several low-confidence claims (0.12–0.24) regarding notified body designation timelines and the Annex VII mandatory-use scope should be treated cautiously, as they rely on undated industry blogs rather than authoritative legal text.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source confirms how many notified bodies have been formally designated specifically under the AI Act as of the current date. It remains unclear whether COM(2025) 836 has been adopted and how it relates to the existing Article 35 mechanism. The interplay between Annex I sectoral conformity assessment (e.g., MDR) and AI Act-specific Annex VI/VII procedures for dual-regulated products requires further clarification, as does whether notified body capacity will be sufficient by the August 2026 deadline.
